attributes.title: Level 4

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the enemy sprite name first, and the player sprite second in the [set sprite follow] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: ❓ What is the sprite name of the Enemy sprite? What is the sprite name of the Player sprite?

Solution: The red bubbles in the [set sprite follow] block should be changed to “pirate” and “pirateShip.”
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code.


Fix the bugs in the code so the Enemy sprite follows the Player sprite!

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Get ready for a tropical adventure, but beware of the pirates along the way!

validationItems.failureText: Check that the correct sprite names have been selected in the [set sprite follow] block.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Did you change the Enemy’s follow speed so that it does not move too fast?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓Did you try different numbers inside the parameter bubble?


Solution: The speed parameter in the [set sprite follow] block is decreased to a number lower than 100 (the default setting).
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, the Enemy sprite moves so quickly that it’s impossible to move the Player sprite to the Goal.


Fix the bugs in the code so the Enemy sprite follows the Player sprite more slowly.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Get ready for a tropical adventure, but beware of the pirates along the way!

validationItems.failureText: Check that the speed parameter in the [set sprite follow] block is a number that is challenging but not impossible.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select different sprite kinds in the second blue bubble of each of the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja:

❓ What do you want to happen when the player sprite overlaps with the goal sprite? The enemy sprite? The food sprite?


Solution: The otherSprite Player sprite kinds in the [on sprite overlaps sprite] containers should be replaced with “Goal,” “Enemy,” and “Food.”
steps.instructions:
When the player sprite overlaps other sprites, nothing happens!


Fix the bugs in the code so the [on sprite overlaps sprite] container blocks make the game work as expected.

subgroups.title: Debugging Sprite Kinds and Parameters

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Get ready for a tropical adventure, but beware of the pirates along the way!

validationItems.failureText: Check that the correct sprite kinds have been selected in the second blue bubble of each [on sprite overlaps sprite] container block.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of White Belt! Before you create your final White Belt project, there are a few neat tricks to learn that could take your game to the next level! In this level, you’ll learn about functions, which are chunks of code that run whenever they are called. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 4:

badges.title: Function Junction
badges.description: Use functions to make something happen at different points in a project.

badges.title: A Whole New Kind of Sprite
Making a Connection
badges.description: Make something happen when 2 different sprites overlap.

badges.title: Right Behind You
badges.description: Set one sprite to follow another sprite.

badges.title: Make It Dazzle
badges.description: Add an effect to any sprite.

badges.title: The End of the Road
badges.description: End the game in a win or loss when something happens in a project.
